'''Chikako Mese''' is an American mathematician known for her work in [[differential geometry]], geometric analysis and the theory of [[harmonic map]]s. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Johns Hopkins University]].{{r|jhu}}

==Education and career==
Mese graduated from [[Elk Grove High School (Elk Grove Village, Illinois)]] in 1987.{{r|d214}} As a [[softball]] player at Elk Grove, she broke the national record for the number of runs scored in a season, with 69 runs.{{r|runs|ihsa}} Although primarily a catcher, she played in seven different positions for her team, and also tied the state record for the most walks in a season, 35.{{r|walks|ihsa}}

She earned a bachelor's degree in 1991 from the honors program at the [[University of Dayton]], majoring in mathematics,{{r|hi}} and
completed a Ph.D. in mathematics at [[Stanford University]] in 1996. Her dissertation, ''Minimal Surfaces and Conformal Mappings Into Singular Spaces'', was supervised by [[Richard Schoen]].{{r|mg}}

Before joining the Johns Hopkins University faculty in 2004 as an associate professor,{{r|simons}} she held assistant professorships at the [[University of Southern California]] and [[Connecticut College]].{{r|hi}} At Johns Hopkins, she became the first tenured female mathematician.{{r|d214}} She was promoted to full professor in 2007, and chaired the mathematics department from 2008 to 2011.{{r|simons}}

==Recognition==
In 2007, Elk Grove High School recognized Mese as a distinguished alumna.{{r|d214}}
She was named a Simons Fellow by the [[Simons Foundation]] in 2017.{{r|simons}}
She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 Class, for "contributions to the theory of harmonic maps and their applications, and for service to the mathematical community".{{r|fams}}
